claim: All cats have tails. Max is a cat. So Max has a tail.

steps.text: All cats have tails.
Max is a cat.
So Max has a tail.

hints: A 'Given' is something the problem tells you is true.
The last step takes the rule about all cats and uses it on one cat.

claim: Adding two even numbers always gives an even number.

steps.text: An even number is made of pairs with none left over.
Take two even numbers, each made only of pairs.
Putting them together still leaves no odd one out.
So the total is even.

hints: Start with what the word 'even' means.
The last step should say the same thing as the claim.

claim: The angles inside a triangle add to 180°.

steps.text: Draw a line through one vertex parallel to the opposite side.
The two outer angles equal the two far angles of the triangle.
steps.reason: Alternate angles on parallel lines are equal

steps.text: Those three angles sit on a straight line.
steps.reason: Angles on a straight line add to 180°

steps.text: So the triangle's three angles add to 180°.

reasons: Alternate angles on parallel lines are equal
Angles on a straight line add to 180°
hints: The first step draws a new line. Drawing something new is called a construction.
Find the step about a straight line: angles on a straight line add to 180°.

claim: There is no largest prime number.

steps.text: Suppose there were a largest prime, and list every prime up to it.
Multiply them all together and add 1. Call the result N.
N leaves remainder 1 when divided by any prime on the list.
So N has a prime factor not on the list, or is itself prime.
Either way there is a prime beyond the supposed largest — a contradiction.

hints: This proof starts by pretending the opposite is true.
It ends by showing the pretend idea can't be right.

claim: 1 + 2 + ... + n = n(n+1)/2 for every whole number n ≥ 1.

steps.text: Check n = 1: the left side is 1 and the right side is 1(2)/2 = 1.

choices: Assume the formula holds for some n = k.
Assume the formula holds for every n at once.
Check n = 2 and conclude it always works.

steps.text: That simplifies to (k+1)(k+2)/2, which is the formula for n = k+1.
So it holds for 1, and whenever it holds for k it holds for k+1.

hints: Induction has two parts: a first case, and a step from k to k + 1.
Before you can go from k to k + 1, you need to suppose it works for k.
